note: No version. The version is bound into the ciphertext, so a request without one is asking for a record that cannot be bound to where it will live — and there is no defaulting that would be honest, because only the caller knows which write shape it is about to use.
A negative version. Versions are assigned from a monotonic counter that starts at 1, and `0` is the create-only precondition — nothing below that names a record that can exist.
No plaintext. Sealing nothing is not a coherent request; the member is the whole input.

The record's parts sent separately. Splitting title/body/tags would let a host read the shape of the material from ciphertext lengths — the sealed tiers seal one blob for exactly this reason, so the structure belongs inside `plaintext`, not beside it.
Bare/unnamespaced ext key — SPEC §4.5.1 requires every immediate child of ext to be reverse-DNS namespaced.
